Each proposal below is a protocol. It states a hypothesis, what would falsify it, the unit of
analysis, the data source with a call that proved the source reachable, and the analysis in R,
and it is published in that state before any analysis is run.

The order matters and it is deliberate. A protocol written after the result is known is not a
protocol, and a project that criticizes selective reporting cannot itself decide what its
question was once it has seen the answer. Every proposal therefore carries a date and a status,
and a result page will link back to the protocol as it stood.

## Status values

The distinction between a design and a protocol is not cosmetic. It comes from the sibling
project's `studies/DESIGN-STANDARD.md` and it is the rule this project now works to: **the
difference between a design and a protocol is a set of computed numbers.** A document that
asserts its sample size, its power or its feasibility rather than measuring them is a design,
whatever it calls itself.

| status | meaning |
|---|---|
| `design` | the question, hypothesis, threats and probes are written. Feasibility is not yet measured |
| `protocol-pending-validation` | probes computed and written in. One or more validation gates need human labels before it runs |
| `protocol-reduced` | probes computed, and they came back small enough that a pre-written rule cut the analysis down |
| `agenda` | a real gap that public data cannot answer, recorded rather than skipped |
| `reported` | result published with the protocol and, when they exist, the reviews |

Nothing here is `registered`. Registration needs the probes complete, the validation gates
passed, and two reviews attached. No document has all three.

## Where each one stands

| | question | status | what is blocking it |
|---|---|---|---|
| **P01v2** | Does advocating transparency predict practicing it? | protocol | screening and grading labels, then review |
| **P02** | Does meta-research cite retracted work? | protocol | shares P01v2's screening gate |
| **P03** | Is bad news cited more? | protocol | 300 abstracts classified by the author |
| **P05** | Do the links actually resolve? | protocol | a requester bug, then 100 hand checks |
| **P06** | Do conclusions soften between preprint and journal? | protocol, reduced | 141 pairs found, so the ordinal outcome was cut to binary by a pre-written rule |
| **P07** | When two studies measure the same thing, do they agree? | design | nobody has counted the pairs yet |
| **P08** | Do meta-research studies follow the guidelines they audit by? | design | scoring STROBE needs a human reading 150 articles |
| **P09** | Does meta-research change the practice it documents? | design | the author must choose which documented problems count |
| **P04** | The field is observational about itself | agenda | needs a journal or funder willing to randomize |

## Review

Nothing here has been reviewed. Review is by two models from different providers, each given the
document and instructed to refute it, with output validated against a schema and adjudicated by
the fixed rule in `build/audit/adjudicate.py`. That rule downgrades an unsubstantiated severe
finding rather than counting it, lets a lone reviewer holding a verbatim quote block a document
two others called sound, and publishes a contested document as contested rather than picking a
winner. Twelve golden cases pin it.

No document is reviewed by one model alone. The Codex account's usage limit was exhausted on
2026-09-16 and resets on 2026-09-20, so reviews begin then.

The five documents at protocol stage go first. The three designs are reviewed when their probes
complete, because a reviewer asked to assess feasibility numbers that do not exist yet is being
asked to review a wish.

## How these were chosen

The selection rule was to turn the field's own instrument on the field. Meta-research measures
whether others share data, cite retracted work, follow checklists, replicate, and report
inconvenient findings. Those questions had not been asked about meta-research itself, and most
are answerable from data already harvested or openly available.

The rule also kept out the obvious alternative. A study measuring transparency, or FAIRness, in
one more specialty is a rate in a new population, and rates in new populations are what this
corpus already holds in quantity. Every document here has an exposure, an outcome and a
direction, and every one can come out the other way.

One candidate was dropped for lack of novelty rather than lack of interest: a study relating a
journal's transparency policy score to the transparency of the meta-research it publishes. The
corpus search found PMID 37433624, a systematic review with individual participant data
meta-analysis of predictors of data and code sharing, which covers it. It is recorded here
because a dropped idea and the reason it was dropped are part of the trail.

P04 is not runnable and says so. P09 is the most important question of the set and is the least
far along, which is a fact about difficulty rather than about priority.
